newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Annan mulls Bosnia, Albania with Austria leaders.
newsitem.headline: Annan mulls Bosnia, Albania with Austria leaders.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Tuesday reaffirmed the United Nations' commitment to the Dayton peace accords and said Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation must never be allowed to turn into a European Gaza Strip.

In talks with Austrian leaders touching on troublespots in the region, Annan said it was important that war criminals identified in former Yugoslavia be brought to trial to meet the terms of the 1995 peace agreement.
"He said the alternative to the (Moslem-Croat) Federation would be the Gaza Strip on a European level," Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel told reporters after meeting Annan.
"If there is a large Croatia, a large Serbia and something in between, then it could hardly be liveable and could have dramatic negative consequences in the next decades," Schuessel added.
Annan, who is on a three-day visit to Vienna, the seat of several U.N. organisations, also discussed the crisis in Albania with Schuessel.
"We agreed on the need to push for elections. The process (ensuring) that the elections are free and fair must not be interrupted or postponed," Schuessel said.

The poll has been called for June 29 despite continued bickering over the electoral system among Albania's political parties. European leaders have warned they may withdraw assistance if political leaders failed to stick to the date.

Annan was due to meet former Austrian chancellor Franz Vranitzky, who has taken on the job as special envoy to Albania for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to review the current situation in the impoverished Balkan nation.
The U.N. chief was also due to meet Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima before addressing employees at the U.N. headquarters on the banks of the River Danube.
